answer_text: A solenoidd is a cylindricall coil of many closely wound turns of insulated copper wire. When current flows, the field inside is nearly uniform and parallel to the axis, similar to the field of a bar magnet. One end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole, depending on the direction of current (right-hand grip rule). Outside, the field is weak. A soft-iron core placed inside makes a strong electromagnet used in electric bells and cranes.
